correctness.rationale: The exact mod-two degree equations define a 15-dimensional quotient and an explicit formula for all 21-edge Walsh coefficients. The Python certificate exhausts 2^15 inner-edge encodings; a second C++ certificate independently enumerates all 2^21 orientations and checks every quotient Walsh coefficient by direct sums. Both agree on 2640 regular tournaments, 8656 nonzero quotient multipliers, least positive magnitude 16, and the exact kernel sum 1427840. The 64-fold lift yields rank 553984. Translation averaging analytically proves minimality among arbitrary endpoint projections, giving 11155/256. Finite proofs are exhaustive for order seven and not extrapolated.

value.rationale: Regular tournaments are a classical natural constraint family; the seven-vertex case is the first with three unlabelled regular tournament types. The full Walsh support and its sharply minimized endpoint range-projector norm are natural harmonic-analytic invariants not specified by the 2640 cardinality or the first-degree covariance. The unexpectedly large exact norm 11155/256 quantifies the unconditional instability of projecting onto this Fourier range; the exhaustive classification resolves a genuinely natural finite case without claiming a universal-order theorem.
